subject: Climate & Environment
title: The Ocean as a Carbon Sink
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Ocean as a Carbon Sink.

hook.text: The ocean absorbs about 30% of human CO₂ emissions. It's the planet's largest carbon sink.

buildup.text: CO₂ dissolves into seawater at the surface. Cold water absorbs more than warm water.

discovery.text: Phytoplankton also absorb CO₂ through photosynthesis — producing half the world's oxygen.

twist.text: As the ocean warms, it absorbs less CO₂. The carbon sink is weakening just when we need it most.

climax.text: If the ocean stops absorbing carbon, atmospheric CO₂ will rise even faster.

punchline.text: The ocean has been cleaning up after us. It's getting tired.

quiz.question: What happens to the ocean's ability to absorb CO₂ as it warms?

details.summary: The ocean has absorbed about 30 percent of all human-emitted carbon dioxide since industrialization. This uptake slows the pace of atmospheric warming but comes at a cost: absorbed CO2 forms carbonic acid, gradually lowering ocean pH in a process called acidification.
details.whyItMatters: The ocean's carbon sink has bought time against rapid warming, but acidification threatens marine life. Tracking this balance is essential for climate strategy.
takeaways: About 30 percent of human CO2 ends up dissolved in the ocean
Absorbed CO2 forms carbonic acid and lowers ocean pH
Warming may weaken the ocean's future absorption capacity

faq.question: How much carbon dioxide has the ocean absorbed?
faq.answer: Since the Industrial Revolution the ocean has taken up roughly 170 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide. Current estimates suggest it absorbs about 10 billion tonnes per year, though the rate may slow as surface waters warm and saturate.

faq.question: Does the carbon sink benefit or harm the ocean?
faq.answer: It benefits the global climate by reducing atmospheric CO2, but it harms the ocean itself. The resulting acidification weakens shells and coral skeletons, disrupts food webs, and threatens fisheries that billions of people depend on.
